4.text: On another sketch (Fig. 219) three worlds are represented by three

5.text: concentric circles. Our world is the innermost. The Polar Star again stands

6.text: in the centre. On the left hand are the Sun and the Moon. The latter is

7.text: represented as a man holding a lasso, with two human captives standing

8.text: beside him. Between the Sun and the Moon are the stars of Pehiˊttin.¹

9.text: Beneath the Moon is located the black mountain of Darkness. At the

10.text: bottom stands a house made of earth belonging to the keˊlet. Two keˊlet

11.text: walk on all-fours. A large worm² wriggles above the house, its tail armed

12.text: with a long sting. The Left-hand Dawn has a low wooden house with two

13.text: “murderers,”³ one tied on each side. The Genuine Dawn has a house

14.text: raised on a platform, which is supported by a single pole. Four dogs are

15.text: tied on the sides of the house. In the region of the Right-hand Dawn, at

16.text: the left side of the sketch, lives Dawn-Top-Woman (Tñeˊs˙qᴀ-ñe)⁴ in a small

17.text: house, which is also supported on a single pole. Under her feet is Venus.

18.text: The next sketch (Fig. 220a) shows the Moon with the lasso in his

19.text: hand. The captive girl stands by his side. He is displeased with two

20.text: shamans because of the many evil charms they have created, with his aid,

21.text: to destroy other people. He paralyzes them by binding their heads and

22.text: hands with invisible strings, and pulling them upward (Fig. 220, b, c). The

23.text: Moon’s wife is represented with her face half blackened with soot (Fig. 220, d).
